analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the dynamics of H5N1 cross-reactivity in pre-existing antibodies and their relationship with responses to previously circulating influenza strains. By measuring antibody levels in adolescents, adults, and seniors using whole inactivated H5N1 virus, the research reveals that detectable H5N1-reactive antibodies are present in most individuals, regardless of age. A consistent positive correlation is observed between H5N1-reactive antibodies and responses to the H1N1pdm09 strain A/California/7/2009 (CA). The findings suggest that H5N1 cross-reactivity is not strictly age-dependent or imprinting-specific, but rather associated with responses to other strains. papers.title_zh: H5N1及既往流行病毒的抗体谱高度动态化且与年龄和首次感染无关
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The increasing incidence of H5N1 influenza virus transmission from animal species to humans has heightened concerns about an imminent H5N1 pandemic. Prior studies using recombinant hemagglutinin and neuraminidase proteins have reported age-dependent cross-reactivity to H5N1, attributed to immune imprinting from an individual’s first influenza virus exposure. However, whether this pattern holds when using whole inactivated virus (WIV), capturing antibodies against diverse viral proteins, and is stable over time remains unknown. We therefore aimed to determine whether H5N1 cross-reactivity of pre-existing antibodies to whole virus follows an age-dependent or imprinting-specific pattern, and whether this pattern is stable over a five-year period. To this end, we measured serum antibody levels in adolescents, adults and seniors by ELISA using whole inactivated H5N1 virus as antigen rather than purified proteins. Detectable, albeit generally low, levels of H5N1-reactive antibodies were present in most individuals, irrespective of age. Comparison of antibody levels against H5N1 with those to five historical influenza virus strains revealed a consistent positive correlation between H5N1-reactive antibodies and responses to the H1N1pdm09 strain A/California/7/2009 (CA), across all age groups. Using unbiased clustering of antibody titers against H5N1, CA, and the H3N2 strain A/Perth/16/2009 (PE), we identified seven distinct age-transcending antibody profiles. These profiles covered individuals with varying titers to all three included viruses but also identified individuals with high anti-CA levels, yet low anti-H5N1 levels and vice versa. Moreover, despite stable antibody levels over a five-year interval in the study population, individual antibody levels and profiles fluctuated considerably over this period. Taken together, our results confirm the presence of H5N1-reactive antibodies in human sera and their association with previously circulating strains. However, they also caution against inferring antibody levels against a new strain based solely on responses to antigenically related strains and highlight the limitations of extrapolating immune status from single timepoint measurements.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 H5N1流感病毒从动物种群向人类的发病率持续增加,引发了对即将到来的H5N1大流行的担忧。此前使用重组血凝素和神经氨酸酶蛋白的研究已报道H5N1的年龄依赖性交叉反应性,并将其归因于个体首次流感病毒暴露所致的免疫印记。然而,当使用全灭活病毒(WIV)并捕获针对多样化病毒蛋白的抗体时,以及这种模式是否随时间保持稳定,目前仍不清楚。因此,我们旨在确定既往抗体对全病毒的H5N1交叉反应性是否遵循年龄依赖或印记特异性模式,以及该模式在五年内是否稳定。为此,我们通过ELISA测定了青少年、成人和老年人血清中针对全灭活H5N1病毒(而非纯化蛋白)的抗体水平。检测到尽管总体水平较低,但大多数个体体内存在可检测的H5N1反应性抗体,且不受年龄影响。将H5N1反应性抗体水平与五株历史流感病毒株的抗体水平进行比较,发现H5N1反应性抗体与H1N1pdm09株A/加利福尼亚/7/2009(CA)的反应之间存在一致的正相关性,且跨所有年龄组。通过对H5N1、CA及H3N2株A/珀斯/16/2009(PE)抗体滴度的无偏聚类分析,我们识别出七种不同的跨年龄抗体谱。这些谱系涵盖了对三种病毒抗体滴度各异的个体,同时也识别出部分个体具有高抗CA水平但低抗H5N1水平,反之亦然。此外,尽管在研究人群中五年内抗体水平保持稳定,但个体抗体水平和谱系在此期间仍出现显著波动。综上所述,我们的结果证实人血清中存在H5N1反应性抗体及其与既往流行株的关联。然而,这些结果也提醒我们,切勿仅基于对抗原相关株的反应来推断新病毒株的抗体水平,并强调了从单一时间点测量结果外推免疫状态的局限性。

papers.title: Respiratory pandemic risk in the Anthropocene: A One Health framework and GISRS+ agenda
papers.abstract: Recent epidemics and pandemics caused by respiratory viruses, alongside the animal panzootic spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5Nx), have become a structural feature of the Anthropocene, yet responses remain largely reactive. This review integrates findings from WHO's Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) and related surveillance data (2000–2024), epidemiological studies of influenza A virus, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and H5Nx, and One Health literature. We examine major groups of respiratory viruses and identify mismatches between risk and surveillance by focusing on spillover potential from animal hosts, human-to-human transmission and its controllability, and Anthropocene characteristics that increase epidemic risk. The analysis indicated that SARS-related coronaviruses and influenza A viruses, particularly H5Nx, are among the leading candidates based on currently available evidence because they have large reservoirs in animal hosts and spillover to humans is highly probable. The previous presymptomatic spread of SARS-CoV-2 and recent mammalian adaptation in H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b highlight limitations of the traditional symptom-based and pathogen-specific surveillance system. Spillover events tend to occur in tropical and subtropical regions in low- and middle-income countries, but most genomic surveillance is in high-income countries. We propose interventions that address the upstream, midstream, downstream processes of epidemics. Upstream interventions are primary prevention measures related to land use, livestock, wildlife, and urban environments; midstream interventions are GISRS+-based pathogen-agnostic genomic and metagenomic early warning systems triggered by One Health; and downstream interventions include vaccines, antivirals, non-pharmaceutical interventions, and engineering with equity-centred global governance and sustainable financing.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores respiratory pandemic risk in the Anthropocene, emphasizing avian influenza A viruses as key targets. It integrates data from WHO's GISRS and related surveillance systems, highlighting the role of animal hosts and spillover potential in pandemic emergence. The review proposes a tiered intervention strategy, including upstream prevention, midstream early warning systems, and downstream measures like vaccines and equitable governance, to address pandemic risk comprehensively.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是人类世的呼吸道大流行风险,特别是检查 禽流感 A 病毒及其引起人畜共患感染的可能性。它解决了近期流行病和大流行的结构特征,包括高致病性禽流感 A(H5Nx)的传播,并通过分析跨物种溢出潜力、人与人之间的传播和增加流行病风险的人类世特征来评估风险与监测之间的不匹配。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了世卫组织全球流感 监测 和响应系统 (GISRS) 和相关 监测 数据(2000-2024 年)的研究结果、甲型流感病毒、SARS-CoV、MERS-CoV、SARS-CoV-2 和 H5Nx 的流行病学研究以及 One Health 文献。它使用系统的方法来分析证据,重点关注动物 宿主 的作用以及病毒在大流行风险中的特征。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 分析表明,SARS 相关冠状病毒和甲型流感病毒,特别是 H5Nx,由于其大型动物 宿主 储存宿主 以及对人类的 跨物种溢出 可能性很高,因此属于大流行风险的主要候选病毒。该审查强调了在评估大流行风险时考虑 跨物种溢出 潜力、人与人之间的 传播 和人类世因素的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,SARS-CoV-2 之前的症状前传播和最近 H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 中哺乳动物的适应揭示了传统的基于症状和病原体特异性 监测 系统的局限性。此外,报告指出,尽管跨物种溢出事件经常发生在低收入和中等收入国家的热带和亚热带地区,但基因组监测主要在高收入国家进行。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了针对流行病上游、中游和下游过程的干预措施。上游干预措施侧重于与土地利用、牲畜、野生动物和城市环境相关的一级预防措施。中游干预措施包括由 One Health 触发的基于 GISRS+ 的病原体不可知基因组和宏基因组早期预警系统。下游干预措施包括疫苗、抗病毒药物、非药物干预措施以及以股权为中心的全球治理和可持续融资工程。

papers.title: Tradeoffs between targeted and expanded testing strategies for influenza A(H5N1)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In a recent article in ASM Case Reports , G. (ASM Case Rep 2:e00165-25, 2025, https://doi.org/10.1128/asmcr.00165-25 ) describe one confirmed and one probable case of influenza A(H5N1) detected through universal subtyping of influenza A-positive specimens, including cases without known animal exposure. These findings highlight the limitations of exposure-based testing strategies and raise important questions about early detection of emerging pathogens. Drawing on lessons from prior pandemics, this commentary examines the tradeoffs between targeted and expanded surveillance and emphasizes the need for adaptive, flexible approaches to laboratory preparedness.

source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT In a recent article in ASM Case Reports , G. (ASM Case Rep 2:e00165-25, 2025, https://doi.org/10.1128/asmcr.00165-25 ) describe one confirmed and one probable case of influenza A(H5N1) detected through universal subtyping of influenza A-positive specimens, including cases without known animal exposure. These findings highlight the limitations of exposure-based testing strategies and raise important questions about early detection of emerging pathogens. Drawing on lessons from prior pandemics, this commentary examines the tradeoffs between targeted and expanded surveillance and emphasizes the need for adaptive, flexible approaches to laboratory preparedness.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,实验室防备工作需采用适应性与灵活性策略,并强调扩大化检测对早期识别甲型(H5N1)流感等新发病原体的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对甲型流感(H5N1)制定更有效的 监测 策略提供信息,从而改善对新出现的人畜共患威胁的早期检测和响应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于有限数量的 病例报告 和之前的大流行经验教训,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。由于分析仅具有抽象性质,因此证据强度适中。

papers.title: Three-Phase Decline in Reported Farm-Level Fowl Typhoid Occurrence in the Republic of Korea, 2000–2024: Temporal Alignment with the 2016–2017 H5N6 HPAI Epidemic
papers.abstract: This study characterized the long-term changes in reported farm-level fowl typhoid occurrence in the Republic of Korea from 2000 to 2024. Farm-level notification records (n = 1495) were obtained from the national livestock disease database. Annual counts were analyzed on a log(count + 1) scale using segmented linear regression. The number of breakpoints was selected by Bayesian information criterion (BIC) comparison of candidate segmented models, and BIC favored a two-breakpoint model. Breakpoints were estimated at 2009.0 (95% CI, 2004.7–2013.3) and 2016.5 (95% CI, 2014.1–2019.0). Phase 1 (2000–2009) declined significantly (annual percent change [APC], −16.3%; 95% CI, −25.9 to −5.5), Phase 2 (2009–2016) showed no significant change (APC, 3.7%; 95% CI, −10.3 to 20.0), and Phase 3 (2016–2024) showed an accelerated decline (APC, −28.0%; 95% CI, −34.9 to −19.8). Province-specific post-2016 slopes were not associated with cumulative provincial HPAI events during 2014–2024 (Spearman’s ρ = −0.143, p = 0.736). The post-2016 acceleration temporally overlapped with the 2016–2017 H5N6 HPAI epidemic, but the study did not measure the contemporaneous interventions or denominators needed for causal attribution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to characterize the long-term changes in reported farm-level fowl typhoid occurrence in the Republic of Korea from 2000 to 2024, with a focus on understanding the temporal patterns of disease decline.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Farm-level notification records (n = 1495) were obtained from the national livestock disease database, covering the period from 2000 to 2024. The study analyzed annual counts of fowl typhoid occurrences across this timeframe.
analysis.methods: Annual counts were analyzed on a log(count + 1) scale using segmented linear regression. The number of breakpoints was selected by Bayesian information criterion (BIC) comparison of candidate segmented models.

The findings suggest potential implications for avian influenza surveillance and control strategies, though the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of direct causal measurements. The study used segmented linear regression and Bayesian information criterion (BIC) to determine breakpoints, providing a structured analysis of the temporal trends in disease occurrence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述2000年至2024年韩国养殖场级禽伤寒报告发生率的长期变化,重点关注疾病下降的时间模式。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 从国家家畜疫病数据库获取了1,495份养殖场级通报记录,覆盖2000年至2024年。本研究分析了该时间段内禽伤寒发生率的年发病数。
elements_zh.methods: 年发病数以log(发病数+1)为尺度,采用分段线性回归进行分析。通过贝叶斯信息准则(BIC)比较候选分段模型,确定断点数量。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to characterize the long-term changes in reported farm-level fowl typhoid occurrence in the Republic of Korea from 2000 to 2024, with a focus on understanding the temporal patterns of disease decline.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: Farm-level notification records (n = 1495) were obtained from the national livestock disease database, covering the period from 2000 to 2024. The study analyzed annual counts of fowl typhoid occurrences across this timeframe.
analysis_en.methods: Annual counts were analyzed on a log(count + 1) scale using segmented linear regression. The number of breakpoints was selected by Bayesian information criterion (BIC) comparison of candidate segmented models.
analysis_en.main_results: Phase 1 (2000–2009) declined significantly (annual percent change [APC], −16.3%; 95% CI, −25.9 to −5.5), Phase 2 (2009–2016) showed no significant change (APC, 3.7%; 95% CI, −10.3 to 20.0), and Phase 3 (2016–2024) showed an accelerated decline (APC, −28.0%; 95% CI, −34.9 to −19.8).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified a three-phase decline in fowl typhoid occurrence, with the most significant acceleration in the post-2016 period, which temporally aligned with the H5N6 HPAI epidemic.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential link between the H5N6 HPAI epidemic and the decline in fowl typhoid, which could inform surveillance and control strategies for avian influenza viruses.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not measure contemporaneous interventions or denominators needed for causal attribution, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of direct causal evidence.

papers.title_zh: 2000–2024年韩国养殖场级禽伤寒报告发生率的三阶段下降:与2016–2017年H5N6高致病性禽流感流行的时间对齐
papers.source_body_en: This study characterized the long-term changes in reported farm-level fowl typhoid occurrence in the Republic of Korea from 2000 to 2024. Farm-level notification records (n = 1495) were obtained from the national livestock disease database. Annual counts were analyzed on a log(count + 1) scale using segmented linear regression. The number of breakpoints was selected by Bayesian information criterion (BIC) comparison of candidate segmented models, and BIC favored a two-breakpoint model. Breakpoints were estimated at 2009.0 (95% CI, 2004.7–2013.3) and 2016.5 (95% CI, 2014.1–2019.0). Phase 1 (2000–2009) declined significantly (annual percent change [APC], −16.3%; 95% CI, −25.9 to −5.5), Phase 2 (2009–2016) showed no significant change (APC, 3.7%; 95% CI, −10.3 to 20.0), and Phase 3 (2016–2024) showed an accelerated decline (APC, −28.0%; 95% CI, −34.9 to −19.8). Province-specific post-2016 slopes were not associated with cumulative provincial HPAI events during 2014–2024 (Spearman’s ρ = −0.143, p = 0.736). The post-2016 acceleration temporally overlapped with the 2016–2017 H5N6 HPAI epidemic, but the study did not measure the contemporaneous interventions or denominators needed for causal attribution.

papers.title: A neuraminidase-targeting nanobody as a therapeutic candidate against influenza A and B viruses.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses continue to pose a significant threat to human and animal health. However, the limited number of licensed antivirals is increasingly compromised by drug resistance driven by high mutation rates. This highlights the urgent need for broad-spectrum therapeutics with novel mechanisms of action. Nanobodies, a new generation of antibody drugs, have great potential in the treatment of influenza virus infections. Neuraminidase (NA) mediates the sialic acid cleavage required for viral release, and its genetic drift is generally slower than that of hemagglutinin (HA) in influenza viruses, making it an attractive target for broad-spectrum antiviral and vaccine development. To construct a phage display nanobody library targeting NA, an alpaca was immunized with the NA protein of the H9N2 influenza virus. A specific nanobody, designated F4, was subsequently screened from the immune library. The nanobody was engineered into an Fc-fused nanobody, F4-Fc, which exhibited inhibitory activity against multiple influenza A and B viruses in vitro and provided robust prophylactic and therapeutic protection against influenza A and influenza B virus infections in vivo . Mechanistically, F4-Fc inhibits NA enzymatic activity and mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. In conclusion, F4-Fc demonstrates prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy against influenza A and B viruses, representing a promising antiviral drug candidate for influenza virus infection. IMPORTANCE Influenza viruses seriously threaten human and animal health, and drugs are crucial for controlling influenza outbreaks. However, the limited variety of existing anti-influenza virus medicines and the high mutation rate of the virus have led to the continuous emergence of drug-resistant strains. Neuraminidase (NA) is a critical surface glycoprotein that exhibits slower antigenic drift than hemagglutinin (HA), making it an attractive target for cross-protective antiviral development. However, broadly active NA-targeting nanobodies, particularly those effective against both influenza A and B viruses, remain limited. Here, we constructed an Fc-fused F4 nanobody (F4-Fc) targeting neuraminidases from multiple influenza A and B viruses and demonstrated its antiviral efficacy in vitro and protective activity in vivo , highlighting its potential as a promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of influenza virus infection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流感病毒继续对人类和动物健康构成重大威胁。然而,获批的抗病毒药物数量有限,且因病毒高突变率导致的耐药性不断增加,这凸显了对具有新作用机制的广谱治疗药物的迫切需求。

papers.title_zh: 一种靶向神经氨酸酶的纳米抗体作为流感A和B病毒的治疗候选药物
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Influenza viruses continue to pose a significant threat to human and animal health. However, the limited number of licensed antivirals is increasingly compromised by drug resistance driven by high mutation rates. This highlights the urgent need for broad-spectrum therapeutics with novel mechanisms of action. Nanobodies, a new generation of antibody drugs, have great potential in the treatment of influenza virus infections. Neuraminidase (NA) mediates the sialic acid cleavage required for viral release, and its genetic drift is generally slower than that of hemagglutinin (HA) in influenza viruses, making it an attractive target for broad-spectrum antiviral and vaccine development. To construct a phage display nanobody library targeting NA, an alpaca was immunized with the NA protein of the H9N2 influenza virus. A specific nanobody, designated F4, was subsequently screened from the immune library. The nanobody was engineered into an Fc-fused nanobody, F4-Fc, which exhibited inhibitory activity against multiple influenza A and B viruses in vitro and provided robust prophylactic and therapeutic protection against influenza A and influenza B virus infections in vivo . Mechanistically, F4-Fc inhibits NA enzymatic activity and mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. In conclusion, F4-Fc demonstrates prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy against influenza A and B viruses, representing a promising antiviral drug candidate for influenza virus infection. IMPORTANCE Influenza viruses seriously threaten human and animal health, and drugs are crucial for controlling influenza outbreaks. However, the limited variety of existing anti-influenza virus medicines and the high mutation rate of the virus have led to the continuous emergence of drug-resistant strains. Neuraminidase (NA) is a critical surface glycoprotein that exhibits slower antigenic drift than hemagglutinin (HA), making it an attractive target for cross-protective antiviral development. However, broadly active NA-targeting nanobodies, particularly those effective against both influenza A and B viruses, remain limited. Here, we constructed an Fc-fused F4 nanobody (F4-Fc) targeting neuraminidases from multiple influenza A and B viruses and demonstrated its antiviral efficacy in vitro and protective activity in vivo , highlighting its potential as a promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of influenza virus infection.

papers.title: Immunogen selection and prior immunity shape antibody breadth following immunisation with avian H5 hemagglutinin
papers.abstract: Avian influenza A viruses pose a persistent zoonotic threat to humans owing to their expanding host range and high case fatality rates. In particular, viruses from the 2.3.4.4b clade of the H5 subtype have now been detected in over 60 mammalian species, raising serious pandemic concerns. Understanding immune recognition of the H5 hemagglutinin (HA) is therefore critical for effective vaccine design and pandemic preparedness. To understand the breadth of cross-recognition induced by different H5 strains, we selected genetically diverse H5 human isolates from 2003-2023 and assessed neutralising antibody responses elicited by adjuvanted recombinant HA protein-based vaccines in C57BL/6 mice. Neutralisation activity of sera was determined against seven H5 HA variants using pseudotyped viruses and a PR8-reassortant virus in micro-neutralisation assays. Our results showed a wide variety of cross-strain neutralisation across H5 HA antigen variants. The conventional vaccine strain A/Indonesia/05/2005 displayed narrow activity against emerging clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, whereas ancestral variants exhibited cross-neutralisation profiles showing a diversity of breath but with limited potency. Polyvalent H5 HA formulations and nanoparticle-displayed H5 HA platforms substantially broadened cross-neutralisation against diverse H5 strains. To examine the impact of pre-existing immunity on H5 vaccine immunogenicity in mouse models, mice were primed with either seasonal influenza infection or quadrivalent influenza vaccine (QIV) prior to H5 HA immunisation. QIV pre-vaccination, but not prior influenza infection, enhanced subsequent neutralizing responses towards A/Fujian-Sanyuan/21099/2017 (clade 2.3.4.4b) H5. Collectively, our results demonstrate that immunogen selection and prior immunity shape antibody breadth following immunisation with avian A(H5) hemagglutinin.

papers.abstract_original: Avian influenza A viruses pose a persistent zoonotic threat to humans owing to their expanding host range and high case fatality rates. In particular, viruses from the 2.3.4.4b clade of the H5 subtype have now been detected in over 60 mammalian species, raising serious pandemic concerns. Neutralisation activity of sera was determined against seven H5 HA variants using pseudotyped viruses and a PR8-reassortant virus in micro-neutralisation assays. Our results showed a wide variety of cross-strain neutralisation across H5 HA antigen variants. The conventional vaccine strain A/Indonesia/05/2005 displayed narrow activity against emerging clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, whereas ancestral variants exhibited cross-neutralisation profiles showing a diversity of breath but with limited potency. papers.title: Mitigation of aflatoxin B1-induced toxicopathology and immunosuppression in broilers using a multimodal antioxidant formulation.
papers.abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) contamination of poultry feed impairs growth, immunity, and organ function, causing substantial economic losses. This study evaluated the protective efficacy of a multimodal, water-soluble antioxidant formulation (HI-RESIST®) against AFB1-induced toxicosis in broiler chickens. A total of 240 one-day-old Indian River broilers were randomized into six groups (n = 40): control, AFB1 (150 μg/kg feed), HI-RESIST® 1 (1 mL/L water), HI-RESIST® 2 (2 mL/L), AFB1 + HI-RESIST® 1, and AFB1 + HI-RESIST® 2. Treatments continued for 35 days. Outcome measures included body weight and feed intake, mortality, relative weights of thymus, bursa, liver, and kidney, innate (carbon-clearance assay) and cell-mediated (avian tuberculin) immune responses, humoral responses (SRBC, HI titers to Newcastle disease virus and H9 avian influenza), hematology (TEC, TLC, PCV, Hb), and serum biochemistry (ALT, AST, GGT, LDH, IL-33, BUN, creatinine, total protein, albumin, globulin), together with gross and histopathology of thymus, bursa, liver, and kidney. Dietary AFB1 produced the expected picture of aflatoxicosis: reduced feed intake and body weight gain, increased mortality, lymphoid organ involution, suppressed phagocytic and lymphoproliferative responses, lower antibody titers, anemia and elevated hepatic/renal biomarkers, and characteristic hepatic and renal histopathology (p < 0.05). HI-RESIST® supplementation ameliorated these effects in a dose-dependent manner; the 2 mL/L dose restored performance, immune parameters, hematobiochemical indices, and tissue morphology toward control values more effectively than 1 mL/L (statistically significant differences versus AFB1; p < 0.05). HI-RESIST® alone showed no adverse effects and, in some endpoints, enhanced immune and growth measures relative to control. In conclusion, HI-RESIST® administered in drinking water (particularly at 2 mL/L) substantially attenuated AFB1-induced immunotoxicity, hepatonephrotoxicity, and growth depression in broilers. These findings support the potential use of multimodal antioxidant supplementation as a practical strategy to mitigate aflatoxicosis in poultry; field validation and mechanistic studies are recommended.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 家禽饲料中的黄曲霉毒素 B1 (AFB1) 污染会损害生长、免疫力和器官功能,造成重大经济损失。本研究评估了多模式水溶性抗氧化剂配方 (HI-RESIST®) 对 AFB1 诱导的肉鸡中毒的保护功效。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 总共 240 只一日龄印度河肉鸡被随机分为六组(n = 40):对照组、AFB1(150 μg/kg 饲料)、HI-RESIST® 1(1 mL/L 水)、HI-RESIST® 2(2 mL/L)、AFB1 + HI-RESIST® 1 和 AFB1 + HI-RESIST® 2。治疗 持续 35天。
elements_zh.methods: 结果测量包括体重和采食量、死亡率、胸腺、法氏囊、肝脏和肾脏的相对重量、先天和细胞介导的免疫应答、体液反应、血液学、血清生化以及胸腺、法氏囊、肝脏和肾脏的总体和组织病理学。
elements_zh.main_results: 日粮 AFB1 导致采食量和体重增加减少,死亡率 增加,淋巴器官退化,吞噬细胞和淋巴细胞增殖反应受到抑制,抗体滴度降低,贫血和肝/肾生物标志物升高,以及特征性肝和肾组织病理学 (p < 0.05)。HI-RESIST® 补充剂以剂量依赖性方式改善这些影响;2 mL/L 剂量比 1 mL/L 更有效地恢复性能、免疫参数、血液生化指数和组织形态,使其接近对照值(与 AFB1 相比具有统计学显着差异;p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在饮用水中施用 HI-RESIST®(特别是 2 mL/L)可显着减弱 AFB1 诱导的肉鸡免疫毒性、肝肾毒性和生长抑制。作者得出的结论是,多模式抗氧化剂补充剂可以减轻家禽的黄曲霉中毒。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持多模式抗氧化剂补充剂作为减轻家禽黄曲霉毒素中毒的实用策略的潜在用途。建议进行现场验证和机制研究,以确认商业环境中的有效性和安全性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在特定肉鸡品种和 AFB1 剂量的受控实验环境中进行的,限制了对田间条件的普遍适用性。由于缺乏长期随访且免疫和生化终点可能存在混杂,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Roles of Laboratory Animal Models in Zoonotic Diseases: A Review on Pathogenesis, Transmission, and Prevention Strategies
papers.abstract: Emerging zoonotic diseases have become an increasing concern for global health due to the rising incidence of pathogen transmission from animals to humans. The present study aimed to comprehensively synthesize the current knowledge on zoonotic disease outbreaks and transmission, with a specific focus on evaluating the role, applications, advantages, and limitations of laboratory animal models in this field. A peer-reviewed literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026, supplemented by earlier pivotal studies. The current study evaluated a range of models, including conventional, humanized, and transgenic mice, hamsters, ferrets, guinea pigs, rabbits, non-human primates, and emerging alternatives, focusing on their utility, strengths, and drawbacks for studying host-pathogen interactions, immune responses, tissue tropism, and disease progression. The present study underscored the importance of animal models in the preclinical assessment of antiviral agents, vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and innovative therapeutic strategies. Recent outbreaks caused by pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus, H5N1 influenza virus, Mpox virus, Ebola virus, Marburg virus, hantavirus, and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus have highlighted the urgent necessity to enhance comprehension of zoonotic disease emergence and transmission. The current challenges included species-specific differences, translational limitations, reproducibility, and ethical considerations, as well as emerging alternatives such as organoids, organ-on-chip platforms, and computational modeling, all of which were addressed in the present findings. Integrating advanced animal models with One Health approaches can strengthen disease surveillance and accelerate therapeutic development.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of laboratory animal models in understanding zoonotic diseases, particularly avian influenza A viruses, with an emphasis on pathogenesis, transmission, and prevention strategies. The central question is to evaluate the utility, strengths, and limitations of these models in studying host-pathogen interactions, immune responses, tissue tropism, and disease progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a peer-reviewed literature search in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, including studies published between 2000 and 2026, with supplementary inclusion of earlier pivotal studies. The study design involved evaluating various animal models, including conventional, humanized, and transgenic mice, hamsters, ferrets, guinea pigs, rabbits, non-human primates, and emerging alternatives.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review emphasized the importance of animal models in preclinical assessments of antiviral agents, vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and innovative therapeutic strategies. It also highlighted the need to address challenges such as species-specific differences, translational limitations, reproducibility, and ethical considerations.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identified challenges such as species-specific differences, translational limitations, reproducibility, and ethical considerations as significant issues in the use of animal models. Additionally, it noted the need for further exploration of emerging alternatives like organoids, organ-on-chip platforms, and computational modeling.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggested integrating advanced animal models with One Health approaches to strengthen disease surveillance and accelerate therapeutic development. It also called for continued research into improving the accuracy and applicability of these models for studying zoonotic diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the role of laboratory animal models in studying avian influenza A viruses, focusing on their applications in understanding pathogenesis, transmission, and prevention strategies. The study highlights the importance of these models in preclinical assessments of antiviral agents and vaccines, while also addressing challenges such as species-specific differences and ethical concerns. It underscores the need for integrating advanced models with One Health approaches to enhance disease surveillance and therapeutic development. The review also identifies gaps in current methodologies and suggests the exploration of emerging alternatives like organoids and computational modeling to improve research outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注实验动物模型在了解人畜共患疾病(特别是 禽流感 A 病毒)方面的作用,重点是 发病机制、传播 和预防策略。核心问题是评估这些模型在研究 宿主-病原体相互作用、免疫应答、组织向性和疾病进展方面的效用、优势和局限性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述在 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Google Scholar 中进行了同行评审的文献检索,包括 2000 年至 2026 年间发表的研究,并补充纳入了早期的关键研究。研究设计涉及评估各种动物模型,包括传统、人源化和转基因小鼠、仓鼠、雪貂、豚鼠、兔子、非人类灵长类动物和新兴替代品。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调了动物模型在抗病毒药物制剂、疫苗、单克隆抗体及创新治疗策略临床前评估中的重要性。同时指出需解决物种特异性差异、转化限制、可重复性及伦理考量等挑战。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述将物种特异性差异、翻译限制、可重复性和伦理考虑等挑战确定为动物模型使用中的重大问题。此外,它指出需要进一步探索新兴替代品,如类器官、器官芯片平台和计算模型。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该评论建议将先进的动物模型与 One Health 方法相结合,以强化疾病 监测 并加速治疗开发。它还呼吁继续研究提高这些模型在研究人畜共患疾病方面的准确性和适用性。

papers.title_zh: 实验动物模型在人畜共患疾病中的作用:发病机制、传播 和预防策略的综述
papers.source_body_en: Emerging zoonotic diseases have become an increasing concern for global health due to the rising incidence of pathogen transmission from animals to humans. The present study aimed to comprehensively synthesize the current knowledge on zoonotic disease outbreaks and transmission, with a specific focus on evaluating the role, applications, advantages, and limitations of laboratory animal models in this field. A peer-reviewed literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026, supplemented by earlier pivotal studies. The current study evaluated a range of models, including conventional, humanized, and transgenic mice, hamsters, ferrets, guinea pigs, rabbits, non-human primates, and emerging alternatives, focusing on their utility, strengths, and drawbacks for studying host-pathogen interactions, immune responses, tissue tropism, and disease progression. The present study underscored the importance of animal models in the preclinical assessment of antiviral agents, vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and innovative therapeutic strategies. Recent outbreaks caused by pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus, H5N1 influenza virus, Mpox virus, Ebola virus, Marburg virus, hantavirus, and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus have highlighted the urgent necessity to enhance comprehension of zoonotic disease emergence and transmission. The current challenges included species-specific differences, translational limitations, reproducibility, and ethical considerations, as well as emerging alternatives such as organoids, organ-on-chip platforms, and computational modeling, all of which were addressed in the present findings. Integrating advanced animal models with One Health approaches can strengthen disease surveillance and accelerate therapeutic development.

news.excerpt: Texas A&M poultry science researchers are testing far-UVC light as a potential tool to reduce bird flu and other pathogens in poultry houses.

news.content_title: Texas A&M AgriLife tests far-ultraviolet light to prevent bird flu in poultry
news.content: Skip to main content Skip to footer Events and Learning Latest News Press and Media Search Input AgriLife Today Texas A&M AgriLife's digital magazine and newsroom Environment Farm & Ranch Lawn & Garden Life & Health Science & Tech Around Texas A&M AgriLife Farm & Ranch Life & Health Press Releases Science & Tech Texas A&M AgriLife tests far-ultraviolet light to prevent bird flu in poultry Poultry researchers to study light’s ability to reduce pathogens without harming birds September 3, 2026 - by Karn Dhingra Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... When a strain of highly pathogenic avian influenza, HPAI, tore through U.S. poultry farms in early 2025, farmers culled tens of millions of birds and egg prices soared. The losses highlighted the poultry industry’s urgent need for additional tools and methods to limit the virus’ spread. Now, researchers from the Texas A&M College of Agriculture and Life Sciences are preparing to test a new potential line of defense. They will use a form of ultraviolet light called far-UVC, to see if it can kill HPAI, without harming birds on poultry farms. “The current HPAI outbreak began around 2022 and hasn’t ended,” said Morgan Farnell, Ph.D., avian microbiology and immunology professor, Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service program leader and associate department head in the Texas A&M Department of Poultry Science, “Avian influenza is still being found in Texas wildlife. It is not considered to be endemic in the U.S. and is classified as a reportable poultry disease.” Farnell and Ziteng “Tim” Xu, Ph.D., Texas A&M AgriLife Research smart technologies in poultry production scientist and assistant professor, Department of Poultry Science, will lead the third and final phase of a multiyear study starting in February, examining whether far-UVC light can reduce airborne pathogen loads inside commercial poultry houses. Researchers in the Texas A&M Department of Poultry Science are testing far-UVC light to determine whether it can reduce airborne pathogens in commercial poultry houses without harming birds. (Michael Miller/Texas A&M AgriLife) Testing far-UVC light in real-world conditions Far-UVC light differs from conventional germicidal UV light because it can inactivate viruses and bacteria without penetrating deeply enough to damage human or animal skin and eyes. Far-UVC light is of interest as an anti-pathogen tool because it could be used safely in occupied spaces such as hospitals, clinics, classrooms, restaurants and poultry houses. Researchers from Columbia University Center for Radiological Research and St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital are studying how effective far-UVC light is against pathogens in a specialized isolator. The results established the groundwork for further testing in commercial farm settings. Farnell said. Texas A&M’s role is to determine whether far-UVC performs similarly under commercial conditions. “The isolators used at St. Jude are small and not very representative of the real world,” Farnell said. “We’ll stock birds at commercial density and test it at Texas A&M.” Researchers will use air-sampling equipment to measure indicator organisms, including aerobic bacteria, coliforms and Staphylococcus aureus, before and after far-UVC exposure. Those readings will inform far-UVC’s potential impact on pathogens like HPAI. The Barbara J. Huffman and William M. “Bill” Huffman ’53 Poultry Science Farm Complex, where the trials will be conducted, along with the department’s Biosafety Level 2 laboratory and biosecurity and environmental sampling experience, made the university a natural partner for the project’s applied phase, Farnell said. Measuring how far-UVC works around birds Xu will focus on the engineering challenges of deploying the technology in poultry houses. Dust can absorb or scatter far-UVC light before it reaches spaces occupied by birds. His team will measure how much ultraviolet radiation reaches those areas. Using artificial intelligence-assisted camera tracking, researchers also will monitor whether the light will affect the behavior, circadian rhythms and growth performance in the chickens. Xu is also designing an integrated disinfection system that combines far-UVC air treatment with UVC-enabled positive-pressure ventilation and robotic floor-disinfection modules. The team will test which components are necessary to effectively control pathogens. If the project is successful, researchers could eventually apply the technology beyond poultry facilities to swine and dairy operations, Xu said. A potential new tool for poultry producers The study by Farnell and Xu will span two years and include four flocks, two raised under summer conditions and two under winter conditions. Farnell said the poultry industry needs new tools to protect bird health. The industry has steered away from using antibiotics over the past decade. However, vaccinating for avian influenza is problematic with broilers for a number of reasons. Any tool must maintain flock productivity to make economic sense for farmers, he said. Fewer infections could reduce mortality and economic losses throughout the poultry supply chain. “Anything to improve bird health improves animal welfare and ultimately creates better outcomes for producers,” Farnell said. The project is funded through a $2 million U.S. Department of Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service grant from the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Poultry Innovation Grand Challenge award. news.content: ___ × Market Information Top Poultry Companies Expert Insights Blogs Regions Magazines Sign In Poultry Meat Egg Poultry Health Sustainability Poultry Future Chicken Marketing Summit Poultry Tech Summit Broilers & Turkeys Diseases & Health Avian Influenza Avian influenza reappears in Minnesota turkeys The state had not had any commercial flocks infected since May. Roy Graber September 3, 2026 Budabar | Bigstock Article Summary Highly pathogenic avian influenza has returned to Minnesota commercial poultry, with the USDA confirming the virus in a Wright County turkey flock containing 29,800 birds on September 1, marking the state's 10th commercial flock loss to HPAI in 2026. 29,800 turkeys affected in Wright County commercial flock confirmed positive for HPAI on September 1 This is Minnesota's 10th commercial flock loss to avian influenza in 2026 First HPAI case in over three months after last confirmed case in May in Becker County South Dakota also impacted with three commercial flocks lost in recent weeks across Beadle, Hamlin, and Edmunds counties USDA APHIS and WOAH continue monitoring outbreak; non-commercial flocks do not impact international poultry trade Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has returned to commercial poultry in Minnesota. The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) reported that the presence of the virus was confirmed in a commercial meat turkey flock in Wright County on September 1. There were 29,800 birds involved. The flock infection comes after the state went more than three months with no new cases. The last time HPAI was confirmed in Minnesota was May 20, when a commercial breeder operation in Becker County was struck. This marks the 10th commercial flock in Minnesota to be lost to HPAI in 2026, but only the first for Wright County. The only other state to have the presence of HPAI confirmed in a commercial poultry operation in the past month is South Dakota, which has lost three commercial flocks – one each in the counties of Beadle, Hamlin and Edmunds. The only other state to have the presence of HPAI confirmed in recent weeks is Idaho, but the three affected flocks were not classified by APHIS and the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) as commercial poultry. According to WOAH rules, non-commercial flocks should not impact international poultry trade. To learn more about HPAI cases in commercial poultry flocks in the United States, Mexico and Canada, see an interactive map on WATTPoultry.com. news.title_zh: 禽流感 再次出现在明尼苏达火鸡中
news.source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has returned to Minnesota's commercial poultry industry, with the USDA confirming its presence in a Wright County turkey flock on September 1, 2026. This marks the state's 10th commercial flock loss to HPAI in 2026, and the first for Wright County. The outbreak follows a three-month gap since the last confirmed case in Becker County, South Dakota, in May. The virus was detected in a flock of 29,800 birds, and the USDA and WOAH are monitoring the situation. Non-commercial flocks are not considered in international poultry trade. The outbreak is part of a broader trend, with South Dakota also reporting recent losses in its commercial flocks. No specific response measures are detailed in the evidence, but the situation is under active surveillance.
news.content_zh: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 已重返明尼苏达州商业家禽业,美国农业部于 2026 年 9 月 1 日确认其存在于赖特县火鸡群中。这标志着该州 2026 年第 10 起商业鸡群因 HPAI 死亡,也是莱特县的第一起。自 5 月份南达科他州贝克尔县最后一个确诊病例以来,暴发 出现了三个月的间隔。在 29,800 只鸟群中检测到该病毒,美国农业部和 WOAH 正在监测情况。国际家禽贸易中不考虑非商业鸡群。暴发 是更广泛趋势的一部分,南达科他州最近也报告了其商业鸡群的损失。证据中没有详细说明具体的应对措施,但情况处于积极的监测状态。

August 31, 2026 Farm & Food Care Article Summary Highly pathogenic avian influenza has infected three commercial poultry flocks in South Dakota during August 2024, marking a significant outbreak after the United States had gone nearly a month without commercial flock cases. Three commercial flocks affected: 44,400 meat turkeys in Hamlin County (Aug. 27), 74,900 meat turkeys in Beadle County, and 29,700 birds in a breeder operation in Edmunds County No other state reporting: South Dakota is the only state with confirmed HPAI cases in commercial poultry flocks in August 2024 Previous case: Last commercial flock infection before South Dakota was July 13 in Utah with 275,100 table-egg-laying pullets Backyard poultry: Only South Dakota and Idaho have reported HPAI in backyard poultry, which does not impact global trade under WOAH rules Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) continues to spread in South Dakota, infecting three commercial poultry flocks in August. The most recent case was confirmed Aug. 27 in Hamlin County. In this instance, a flock of 44,400 commercial meat turkeys was affected, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS). Prior to this, HPAI was confirmed in South Dakota in a flock of 74,900 commercial meat turkeys in Beadle County and in a commercial breeder operation in Edmunds County, affecting 29,700 birds. According to APHIS, no other state has had confirmed cases of HPAI in commercial poultry flocks in August, and only two states, South Dakota and Idaho, have had HPAI infections in backyard poultry. Backyard poultry flock infections should not impact global poultry trade, according to World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) rules. Before HPAI was detected in South Dakota, the United States had gone nearly one month without any instances of HPAI in a commercial poultry operation. Outside of South Dakota, the last time a commercial flock was hit by the virus was July 13, when a flock of 275,100 commercial table-egg-laying pullets was struck in Cache County, Utah. news.content_title: Rospticesoyuz explained the registration of chickens by the need to protect against avian flu
news.content: Mandatory registration of poultry will help prevent the spread of outbreaks of avian influenza and increase biosafety. This was announced on September 3 by Galina Bobyleva, Director General of the Rospticesoyuz. "Today, the issue of biosafety is in the first place. Therefore, this measure is absolutely correct, outbreaks are constant, if we talk about the flu," she said in a conversation with NSN . Bobyleva noted that the registration of poultry concerns not only large farms, but also owners of a small number of animals. According to her, even the presence of 10 chickens does not mean that they will be sold, but compliance with the requirements is necessary for safety control. The Russians took the chickens for registration at the MFC. What the law and the government say Starting from September 1, 2026, owners of private subsidiary farms with a population of more than 10 heads of poultry are required to register it in the state information system . The new rules apply to chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys, guinea fowls, quails and ostriches. Against the background of the initiative's introduction, videos appeared on social networks showing Russians bringing their chickens to the MFC for recalculation and registration. However, on September 1, the Rosselkhoznadzor announced that the birds did not need to be transported anywhere . To register, you must contact the state veterinary service at your place of residence. At the same time, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Patrushev instructed the Ministry of Agriculture, the Ministry of Economic Development and the Rosselkhoznadzor to evaluate the regulatory regulation of accounting for animals in private subsidiary farms. The departments will submit proposals to improve the process, taking into account the position of the State Duma and relevant associations. Переведено сервисом « Яндекс Переводчик »
